data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's justification for sustaining §11.3 flags is internally contradictory: it states both critics 'lacked a decidable boundary function' when evaluated against SRC_005, yet also claims 'both verdicts are mechanically void' under school-0 policy. A mechanist policy that voids verdicts precisely BECAUSE the boundary function is absent has already made the threshold decidable — the harness decides abstention by the absence itself. So the boundary the critic says the harness 'cannot inspect' is one the harness mechanically detects. The two halves of the reasoning cannot both be true: either the harness can decide voidness (in which case the flags are not sustained on grounds of indecidability) or it cannot decide voidness (in which case the flags are not mechanically sustained at all).
